title: Shared definitions of the threat model catalogues (threats, recovery actions, mechanisms)

entityClass.description: Name of a class of the setup ontology (table x-classes in SetupOntology.schema.json, drawn in SetupOntology.md); the loader checks it.

category.description: human: acts of people. physical: fire, water, force, environment. supply_chain: tampering before the item reaches the owner. defect: failure, ageing, bugs. software: malicious or faulty software and hosts. randomness: weak or manipulated generation. operational: mistakes and omissions in running the setup. legal: law, courts, authorities. third_party: vendor or provider business risk.

source.description: One cause. environment and owner act without malice; the others are actors against the setup.

phase.description: Lifecycle activity in which a threat can strike.

impactOn.description: Which items are affected, relative to the target entity. The names are defined in the `selectors` table of AccessModel.json; the engine implements only the forms used there (self, placed_in with its options, path, peers).

impactKind.description: destroyed: gone for good. unavailable: cannot be used for now or until some action is taken. disclosed: an attacker obtains a copy or the knowledge. tampered: an attacker changed or replaced it; the rightful people cannot use it, and if it is an active part (device, coordinator, wallet: class flag `active`) the attacker commands it. faulty: wrong by mistake (a transcription error, a wrong policy); the rightful people cannot use it, nobody profits. controlled: the attacker can make the item act as he wants. misused: the holder uses what they can reach or know in an unintended way (impaired judgement); counts as a leak.

origin.description: Review aid: whether the entry comes from the original notes or was added during the completion pass. Can be dropped later.

condition.description: Test on one attribute path. `path` starts at the item under test (or at a bound variable `$x`) and walks attributes as they appear in the plan JSON (`kind`, `items[].format`), follows references into the entities they point to (`seed.devices`), reads `catalog.<column>` of the item's lookup row, the pseudo attributes `class` (with ancestors), `root`, `place`, `container`, and the derived attributes of AccessModel.json. List-valued paths match if any element matches. A missing or blank value never satisfies `in`, `matches`, `eq`, `contains`, `intersects`, `nonempty` or a comparison, and always satisfies `not_in`, `not_matches`, `neq` and `disjoint`. Values of `eq`, `neq`, `contains`, `intersects`, `disjoint` and the comparisons may be `$paths`; `count: true` compares the number of distinct values.

expression.description: A boolean expression over the setup: a condition; a list of conditions (all); {all: [...]}; {any: [...]}; {not: e}; {forall | exists: <class name or $path>, as: '$x', class: <nested class>, where: e}; {can: {agent, action, args, strict}} asks the access module whether an agent (everyone, attacker, {person: $p}, {place: $l}) completes an action; a plain string names a fact of the outcome rules.

predicate.description: A named test that is too structural for a condition (graph or count questions). Implemented by the analysis; the name is the contract.
